content:
As I've written elsewhere and the elephant in the room says, differential geometry in Mathlib is in the unfortunate state that a lot of material is in open PRs, but not available in mathlib. This is a pity (and makes it harder to discover current work, and communicate the current state or build on it). Our aspirations for maximum quality are good, but I wonder if we sometimes let perfect be the enemy of the good.

To give a concrete example, let's talk about properties of immersions (leading up to #29077, i.e. golfing half of a file in the proper way --- fulfilling a promise made one year earlier). This stack of PRs is currently blocked on #28796, whose only (in my impression) outstanding comment is that the results don't need an IsManifold hypothesis, as the relevant charts are contained in the maximal atlas by hypothesis. This is true, yet I don't think it will matter much in applications (which will probably assume a C^k manifold anyway), and this exposes a somewhat large gap in Mathlib (much more results assume IsManifold than having a maximal atlas as hypothesis). Do we need to block progress on immersions on solving this? Or could we put a large and friendly TODO to weaken the hypotheses later, and merge this code now?

FWIW, Javier Gomez Zaragoza is currently trying to remove these hypothesis, I'm helping them. I am optimistic about this one, but don't think it's wise to put a new contributor's work on our "critical path" here.
Of course, I'm happy to be held accountable for fixing this (or helping others fix it).

CC @Floris van Doorn @Oliver Nash @Patrick Massot @Sébastien Gouëzel @Heather Macbeth

In this case a refactor is nice to have, but

  • the status quo is good enough for most things;
  • the refactor won't be very disruptive (in this case: remove some IsManifold assumption in some places).

I'm very happy to merge PRs before doing such a refactor, if they provide a clear TODO.
Such TODOs might actually be quite nice to have: they can be a self-contained project for a beginning Lean user, without really blocking anyone else.
I have just updated #28796 with such TODOs and removed the awaiting-author tag. It's probably good to give this discussion another 24 hours, and then merge if there are no other opinions.
